metadata.title: Student Well-Being and Reading Achievement in PIRLS 2021

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This report uses PIRLS 2021 reading achievement and PIRLS 2021 Student Questionnaire context indicators for fourth-grade students across participating countries and benchmarking entities. The exhibits report international and country-level average reading achievement by well-being indicator categories (e.g., sense of school belonging, bullying frequency), implying use of PIRLS scaling/estimation procedures for achievement scores and questionnaire scale construction. The manuscript does not specify whether complex survey sampling weights (e.g., student/school weights) or replicate weights were applied in the computations shown in the exhibits. Because the analysis is presented as descriptive associations and latent-class profiling (not a predictive ML pipeline), the report should be interpreted as relying on PIRLS-provided scale estimates; analysts using the PIRLS international database should apply the PIRLS complex survey design weights and replicate weights as recommended in the PIRLS 2021 technical documentation when reproducing country estimates.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The report presents associations between questionnaire-based well-being indicators and PIRLS reading achievement, but it does not document how missing questionnaire responses were handled (e.g., exclusion rules or imputation). Given that PIRLS uses complex sampling and questionnaire items/scales, missingness handling can affect the composition of the categorized well-being groups and the resulting average achievement estimates. This omission is a reporting gap for reproducibility, even though the study is primarily descriptive and does not train a predictive ML model.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The report uses PIRLS 2021 fourth-grade students assessed at the end of the school year (and, for some exhibits, also references a delayed assessment of the fourth-grade cohort at the beginning of fifth grade). For each well-being indicator, the exhibits present categorized responses based on PIRLS 2021 Student Questionnaire items/scales (e.g., sense of school belonging scale cut scores; bullying frequency cut scores; collapsed absence categories). The report does not provide explicit inclusion/exclusion rules for missing questionnaire responses or for how students with incomplete scale items were handled; it also does not state whether any additional subsampling (e.g., only students with complete well-being indicators for the ML-LCA profile analysis) was applied beyond the scale construction and the latent-class procedure.

main_findings.performance_metrics: Descriptive statistics only (no ML performance metrics; see outcome_summary)

data.outcome_summary: This PIRLS Insights report uses PIRLS 2021 reading achievement for fourth-grade students and PIRLS 2021 Student Questionnaire indicators to describe how multiple aspects of student well-being relate to reading performance across participating countries. It reports descriptive associations for five individual well-being indicators: sense of school belonging (categorized into High/Some/Little), bullying frequency (Never/Almost Never, About Monthly, About Weekly), feeling tired upon arrival (Never/Every day or almost every day/Sometimes), feeling hungry upon arrival (Never/Sometimes/Every day or almost every day), and frequency of absences (collapsed categories). Across countries, higher belonging and lower bullying and absence frequency are associated with higher average reading achievement, while tiredness and hunger show more complex, non-linear patterns that vary by country. The report also integrates the five indicators using multi-level latent class analysis to form four well-being profile classes and compares their average reading achievement, emphasizing that class proportions differ across countries. Limitations include the lack of documented missing-data handling and the fact that the analyses are not causal; the report explicitly notes that causality is not implied.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is a PIRLS Insights descriptive report rather than an empirical predictive ML study: it presents country-level associations and a latent-class profiling approach (multi-level latent class analysis) without training a supervised ML model and without reporting predictive performance metrics. As a result, fields required for predictive ML extraction (e.g., ML algorithms, target-variable-specific predictive metrics) are not applicable, and the report does not provide a single analytic-sample N or per-country N needed for the schema’s sample breakdown.
